sources.entry: OLIV - Push-to-talk dictation for Thai mixed with English that runs Typhoon Whisper and Gemma on-device with MLX and types English tech words in English instead of Thai script.

summary.one_liner: OLIV is a free, open-source, offline push-to-talk dictation app for Apple Silicon Macs that transcribes Thai mixed with English and types English tech words in English instead of Thai script.
keywords: speech to text for thai tech workers
use_cases: dictating Thai with English tech terms into Slack, VS Code or Notes
offline voice typing on a Mac without sending audio to the cloud
correcting Thai-script spelling of English jargon in speech-to-text output
adding names and jargon to a personal dictionary for dictation
running a self-hosted speech and cleanup server for a team
dictating into terminals and password managers in verbatim mode
how_to_run: Download OLIV.dmg from the project releases, drag OLIV into Applications, and launch it.
Wait for the one-time model download (about 5 GB) on first run.
Hold Right Option, speak, and release the key to paste the text.
Build from source: brew install xcodegen ripgrep, then xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain.
Run bash scripts/build_app.sh to produce build/OLIV.app, and bash scripts/test.sh for tests.
notable: Restores English tech words that were spelled out in Thai script, plus Thai number and ๆ formatting
Fully on-device by default after a one-time model download; cloud engines (Groq, self-hosted OLIV API) are opt-in
Custom Dictionary that guides recognition and applies exact corrections, with CSV import/export
Echo cancellation so music playing on the Mac is not transcribed
Optional self-hostable server and desktop/iOS clients that share the same Rust text pipeline
caveats: Requires an Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or newer) running macOS 14 or later; the Mac app does not run on Intel, Windows or Linux
First run downloads about 5 GB of models from Hugging Face
Accuracy results come from a single speaker (the developer), so other voices and accents are untested
Names and numbers can be wrong even when the meaning matches, so the README advises checking output
